label: Projects
heading: Three questions, mostly about water.
intro: Projects run from the sensor bench to the estuary mudflat. Each one starts with a measurement that does not yet exist.

individual_card_details.heading: Drift, and the half-life of a measurement
individual_card_details.image_alt: Researchers taking field measurements beside a stream
individual_card_details.text: Low-cost turbidity sensors fail slowly. This project builds the calibration records and correction models that let a £300 probe hold its own against a laboratory reference for six months, through a full winter.

individual_card_details.heading: What sediment cores forget
individual_card_details.image_alt: Waves breaking over a rocky coast
individual_card_details.text: Coastal cores are read as archives, but mixing, decay and storm layers erase parts of the record. We are testing how much of a carbon and phosphorus budget survives that loss.

individual_card_details.heading: Microplastics between the road and the river
individual_card_details.text: A two-catchment comparison of tyre wear, road runoff and stream deposition — and why the smallest particles do not behave like the ones we can see.
